title: ATM REST API in Express
idea: The ATM API is the bank's REST service that ATMs call: it opens a session after a PIN check, then debits, confirms or reverses withdrawals in transactions.

analogy.text: A phone line from each branch till to head office. The till reads out a reference number with every request, so a repeated call changes nothing.
analogy.breaks: Head office here is code; it never mishears a reference.

points: Routes call controllers; controllers validate with `zod` and call the service.
The service owns one transaction per call; the repository holds only SQL.
Withdrawals need an Idempotency-Key; a repeat returns 200 and the same transaction.
Domain errors carry a status; one middleware maps every error to JSON.

code.title: Withdraw and reverse
code.caption: Repository, service, controllers and error mapping in one file, on a real PostgreSQL. The ATM sends its request id as the Idempotency-Key header; page 6's request_id column holds it. This trimmed table has no ATM column, so it scopes keys per account; page 6 uses (atm_id, request_id). A session row is seeded; pin.mjs shows how one is created.

walk.text: A trimmed copy of page 6's table; `idempotency_key` plays the role of the request id.
`tx` wraps each service call in BEGIN and COMMIT, or ROLLBACK on error.
Repository: plain SQL, including the account lock and the PENDING-only reverse.
`withdraw`: lock the account, replay a known key, refuse a reused key, else debit.
`reverse` credits back only if the row was still PENDING; otherwise 409.
Controllers parse the header and body with `zod`, then pick 201 or 200.
Error middleware maps validation, domain and unknown errors to status codes.

code.title: PIN check and lockout
code.caption: Opening a session. The PIN is checked against a salted scrypt hash (a demo stand-in for HSM verification), and failures are counted at the bank.

walk.text: Each card stores a random salt and the scrypt hash of its PIN.
Lock the card row; a card with three failures is refused with 403.
A match resets the counter and creates a session.
A miss adds one failure and still commits, so the count survives.
The controller rejects a non-numeric PIN with 400 before any database work.
Try a bad format, wrong and right PINs, then three wrong ones in a row.

pitfalls: Do not throw after counting a failed PIN; the rollback would erase the count.
Scope a key to its ATM or account, and refuse a reused key whose amount differs.
Only 10,000 PINs exist, so a leaked salted hash falls; verify PINs in an HSM.

quiz.q: What does api.mjs print for the second reverse call?
quiz.why: The first call moved TX-1 to REVERSED. The second UPDATE matches no PENDING row, so the service throws a 409.

takeaway: Validate at the edge, decide in one transaction, and replay by Idempotency-Key.

starters: Why is insufficient funds a 409 and not a 400?
How should an ATM authenticate itself to this API?
What should happen if confirm never arrives for a PENDING row?
